negative_reviews.author: Harriet Clegg
negative_reviews.text: Me and my other half used to visit the maki and ramen place in Leeds way before the Meadowhall place opened and we loved it so much we went back multiple times, when we found it the Meadowhall place opened we were so excited we had a place closer to us. But the last couple of times we visited the restaurant in Meadowhall. We have experienced food poisoning and diarrhoea. Please check up on the food safety before you serve it to consumers. But it was not fun taking a day off work because of the food we were served. Thanks

issues: More covers but lower average spend with ramen offers still coming through; sales about the same as last week; a lot saved on labour versus the previous week.
A couple of late prepared Deliveroo orders, otherwise fine.
Labour updated to 20.65% and food cost 24.95%; stock all good.
Reviews: big push on reviews and doing a lot better; a couple of 3 stars, which have been replied to.

Staff: a new part time FOH has been selected; the supervisor trial arranged last week fell through as the applicant withdrew, no other trial is booked, and CVs will be reviewed today with trials arranged and an answer by today or tomorrow. Inka asked for exact updates in the notes rather than 'Eve sorting'.
Compliance a bit lower because of Monday.
An electrician said the fuse board needs an out of hours job as it could fail again at any time; logged as a potential overload in the restaurant (medium) and raised with Inka for a decision.
M14 is the site currently trialling the new performance dashboard.

Region: a new company wide performance dashboard (trialled at M14) will give week on week, month on month and quarter on quarter comparisons; GMs must resolve their outstanding tasks and post updates on it within a week, and Inka will send the link once Michael's guide video is ready.
Region: staff should proactively offer free frozen ramen to students (ask if they are a student, have their ID and have signed up to the app) to lift frozen ramen exposure and Slerp sign ups.
Region: remaining scratch pot vouchers (500 printed) can still be given out until 22/10, crossing out the 23/10 expiry date with a Sharpie.
Region: all bubble tea cups, lids and straws must be ordered only from Boba Box using the product codes shared on Kobas, with flat lids replacing dome lids at marketing's request.

Region: an extra labour margin of up to 2% is allowed for high redemption sites while £5, £3 and 50% off ramen volumes stay high (Nottingham 23%, Leeds 22%), on condition that service and food quality stay high.
Region: food cost may temporarily run toward 30% for two to three weeks while chefs top up to a new baseline par level for key ingredients set by the executive chef team, to stop out of stock items.
Region: managers can tailor the weekly cleaning checklist to their site layout (deadline extended to Friday) and report the changes at the next KPI meeting.
Region: B2B and PR spend should be tracked by opening a Kobas tab named B2B or PR rather than using discount buttons.
Covers rose by 100 (6.04%) week on week while spend per head fell by £0.85 (4.05%).
Sales were up £159.57 (0.44%) week on week but £6,832.37 (15.89%) below target.
The report notes one new FOH starter and new supervisor trials soon; upcoming is the Slerp promo (chase leaflets).
Mall footfall was quiet, and the site is tracking a Christmas parade promotion (AM Updates 21/10).
Deliveroo volume is low at 3 to 5 orders a day, so a single negative review hits the rating hard, and miso cups are spilling in transit (AM Updates 21/10).
A one off customer complaint of food poisoning was received (AM Updates 21/10).
Amy is driving B2B partnerships at Meadowhall (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: Michael made rider wait time the priority delivery metric this week, followed by ratings; sites need a 4.7 Deliveroo rating to compete and open times above 99.5% (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: GMs and head chefs must run a daily morning brief for FOH and BOH using the app's daily tab to review sales, delivery ratings and setups (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: failed delivery orders come from items marked out of stock on Kobas but not on Deliverect, so managers must update both, snooze unavailable extras by PLU and check Deliverect failed order statuses daily (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: stock edit permissions will be suspended for one week to see true variances, after wastage and comps were used to bring variances under 5% and distort Kobas ordering baselines (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: from next week automated Gemini meeting recordings and dashboard sign offs replace manual meeting notes and KPI sheets, with tasks synced to Asana and the legacy spreadsheets kept as a backup for now (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: third party discounted bookings are no longer allowed on Saturdays and are capped at a share of capacity on other days (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: Inka's sites generated around £6,000 of free ramen discounts, and FOH training days are scheduled across Nottingham, Leicester, Meadowhall and Manchester (AM Updates 21/10).
